summary_paragraph: A 65-year-old male with a history of type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and end-stage renal disease status post left renal transplant was admitted for progressive fatigue, lower extremity edema, nausea, diarrhea, and worsening kidney function. Initial evaluation revealed acute on chronic renal failure with elevated creatinine and microcytic anemia. Renal ultrasound showed no obstruction or abnormalities in the transplanted kidney. The patient received two units of packed red blood cells and IV fluids, with improvement in hemoglobin and symptoms. His antihypertensive regimen was adjusted due to renal dysfunction, including discontinuation of valsartan and transition to metoprolol and nifedipine, with addition of furosemide. Tacrolimus dose was reduced due to high trough levels, and calcitriol was initiated for secondary hyperparathyroidism. Diarrhea and nausea resolved with supportive care. He was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up arranged for blood pressure and kidney function monitoring.
